answer.rationale: c2 shows the low-cost vendor path worked sharply on unit cost with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. c6 shows multi-year terms unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service. c4 shows renegotiation recovered margin against market rates, but the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, which blocks that lever. With finance demanding an 18% cut, a 14-day expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, I cannot afford a full primary switch. The lowest-cost-of-ownership path is to run a small, guarded test order with the low-cost vendor to validate continuity before scale, while using the c6 playbook to negotiate a short-bridged extension with the incumbent so the expiry does not force a bad switch. This is the only decision I can take this cycle; everything else waits for the next review.
